_contract: DRAFTS awaiting the operator's seal - Nestor's draft tier, applied to law. Each entry was queued by running the fleet's sealed record against the other sessions' new pieces (2026-08-05): standing law had no answer within reach, so these are proposals. author is the machine; verified_by is EMPTY and stays empty until a person seals the entry by moving it into fleet.json with their name on it. The machine proposes; it does not ratify its own proposals - which is, fittingly, proposal one.

proposed_decisions.question: May a model verify, rule, seal, or publish?
proposed_decisions.commitment: no - a model may propose; only a person may verify, rule, seal, or publish
proposed_decisions.reason: the fleet's most load-bearing principle exists everywhere as prose (CLAUDE.md 0.2, intake_desk_spec 4.1, promote_check verified_by != author, Nestor's seal, the fourth-store narrative) and nowhere as a sealed decision - found by asking Nestor, which correctly answered that nobody ever sealed it. The intake desk paid the tuition: a router with a careful vocabulary contract still emitted unearned conclusions through the middle of it, because every rule was about storage and none was about authorship.
proposed_decisions.author: vishwakarma

proposed_decisions.question: May the field recording why a boundary was crossed be free text?
proposed_decisions.commitment: no - a closed set for writers, pinned by a test, permissive for readers
proposed_decisions.reason: convergent law: three sessions fixed this same defect independently in one night (homestead R-7 and I-13, Nestor #32 closed by #33, willow-mcp #280's event_type note) - a control nothing can check is a label, and a typo'd kind is not an event type, it is a row silently absent from every review surface
proposed_decisions.author: vishwakarma

proposed_decisions.question: Must a declared purpose be checkable rather than a label?
proposed_decisions.commitment: yes - a declared purpose is a control, and a control nothing can check is a label
proposed_decisions.reason: homestead's Purpose accepted any non-blank string, so 'x' bought the same lift as 'medical'; the fleet-level generalization is that any declaration which grants reach must be enforceable at the point it grants it
proposed_decisions.author: vishwakarma

proposed_decisions.question: May a subject's testimony be published attributed under their name?
proposed_decisions.commitment: only under its own explicit scope (testimony_publication) - granting it never implies kb_promotion, and granting kb_promotion never implies it
proposed_decisions.reason: attributed testimony and de-identified structure are opposite movements: an oral-history desk publishes the naming as the record ('Names Given Not Chosen') while kb_promotion strips identity for a shared index - one consent must never quietly stand in for the other
proposed_decisions.author: vishwakarma
proposed_decisions.record: libs/subject-consent core.py (the scope's own comment); apps/intake-desk

proposed_decisions.question: Must the governance chain head be anchored outside the database?
proposed_decisions.commitment: yes - hold verify()'s head somewhere the chain's writer cannot reach, and pass it back as expected_head
proposed_decisions.reason: rechain() proves the migration and the forgery are the same operation, so internal consistency alone can never answer 'is this the same chain it was yesterday'; a mirror without an external anchor degrades from 'someone else remembers' to 'someone else has a copy that will agree with whatever it now says'
proposed_decisions.author: vishwakarma
proposed_decisions.record: willow-mcp #280, PR #281; nestor ledger's expected_head precedent

proposed_rejections.question: May a model verify, rule, seal, or publish?
proposed_rejections.option: the model reports 'corroborated by N sources' itself
proposed_rejections.reason: measured, not argued: the intake router's corroboration claims were wrong on 89% of an adversarial pass, including a source that explicitly denied a claim reported as confirming it
proposed_rejections.author: vishwakarma

proposed_rejections.question: May the field recording why a boundary was crossed be free text?
proposed_rejections.option: close the set for readers too
proposed_rejections.reason: an audit trail must never refuse to show what it already recorded - historical kinds that predate the set must verify and extend (nestor #33's reader-permissive half)
proposed_rejections.author: vishwakarma

proposed_rejections.question: Must the governance chain head be anchored outside the database?
proposed_rejections.option: the self-documenting rechain marker suffices on its own
proposed_rejections.reason: a determined operator can delete the marker and relink again; the marker makes a quiet relink loud, only the external anchor makes it detectable
proposed_rejections.author: vishwakarma
